newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin, Kohl held long phone talk Friday.
newsitem.headline: Jospin, Kohl held long phone talk Friday.

text.p: French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin and German Chancellor Helmut Kohl held a "long telephone conversation" on Friday afternoon, an official at Jospin's office said.
It was the first telephone contact between the two since Jospin was appointed Prime Minister last Tuesday.
According to Manuel Valls, Jospin's adviser during the conversation, it lasted about three quarters of an hour and was "very friendly."
Valls said the aim of the telephone conversation was to make contact ahead of a June 13 Franco-German summit in Poitiers, France, and a European Union summit in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17.

He said the conversation showed a desire on the part of the new French Socialist prime minister "to show that the political and diplomatic work undertaken by the two countries for years would continue."
